text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Property developer Multi Development Corp. talks with ABN Amro bank about possibility of bourse flotation in several years' time. (p1)
- Some 30 to 50 pct of all share issues are postponed due to current down-turn on European Stock Exchanges. (p1)
- Dutch unemployment falls fast in Q1, particularly among young people. (p1)
- Amsterdam companies court rules that management and supervisory boards of former bourse-listed investment company Bobel failed in their task. (p1)
- Automation group Management Share opts for high-margin specialist niches. (p3)
- Publisher VNU increases its stake in French publisher Excelsior to 100 percent. (p3)
- Papermaker Crown van Gelder forecasts yet another year of lower profits. (p3)
- Computer giant IBM interested in state-owned computer automation group Roccade, which is to be privatized. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Opposition Christian Democrats' new parliamentary party leader Jaap de Hoop Scheffer clashes with party chairman Helgers on overhaul of the parliamentary party. (p1)
- Investors dump shares in entertainment and television production group Endemol. (p2)
- One shareholder in U.S. bank Standard Federal, to be acquired by ABN Amro bank, accuses ABN Amro of fraud. (p2)
- Dutch natural gas company NAM discovers gas near Kollum in province of Friesland. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Young offenders given community-based sentences as likely to reoffend as those sentenced to jail terms, research shows. (p1)
- Cooperative Rabobank enters Belgian mortgage market. (p25)
- Staff of installation group GTI Holding plans secondary offering of 375,000 GTI shares. (p25)
- FNV and CNV transport unions urge Dutch carrier KLM to pass its dividend as part of Focus 2000 restructuring plan. (p25)
TROUW
- PTT Telecom rival Libertel sees profit in the future after last year's losses of 107 million guilders. (p7)
- Haarlem-based Internet home-page designer Dataplace plans to set up stock exchange on the Internet. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics president Cor Boonstra slams the company's internal disorganisation in a corporate video.
- Industrial unrest mounting amongst Rotterdam port workers; strikes in the pipeline. (p13)
